chunks: Abu Basir narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:
“Indeed, sawm (fasting) is not from food and drink alone.
Indeed, Maryam said, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast,’ meaning silence.
So guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not envy one another, and do not quarrel.
For indeed envy consumes faith just as fire consumes wood.”

key_terms.أَبْصَارَكُمْ: your gazes, meaning one’s eyes and visual restraint
key_terms.أَلْسِنَتَكُمْ: your tongues, meaning one’s speech and verbal conduct
key_terms.الصِّيَامَ: sawm (fasting), understood here as both physical abstinence and moral restraint
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: faith, which is harmed and consumed by envy
key_terms.الْحَسَدَ: envy, condemned here as spiritually destructive
key_terms.صَمْتاً: silence, explaining the intended meaning of the vowed fast of Maryam
key_terms.صَوْماً: a fast; in this context, a vowed abstention associated with silence

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about the deeper meaning and etiquette of fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sawm is not merely abstaining from food and drink, but also restraining the tongue, the eyes, and harmful behavior. It links the fasting person's discipline to moral purification and warns that envy destroys iman just as fire burns wood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1857 - Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he said:
"Fasting is not limited to refraining from food and drink alone.
Indeed, Maryam said, ‘I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful’ (i.e., silence).
So, guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not envy one another, and do not quarrel.
Indeed, envy consumes faith just as fire consumes wood."
